210ced4c40572dcd5bef82fab8c9f5e9.text: Vancouver Canucks forward Jonathan Lekkerimaki, in action Monday, Nov. 16 during an NHL game against the Utah Mammoth at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City. Brock Boeser had a goal and two assists, lifting the visiting Vancouver Canucks to a 3-2 win over the Utah Mammoth in NHL action Monday at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City. Jake DeBrusk and Filip Chytil also scored for the Canucks (5-17-1), with Nikita Tolopilo turning in a strong performance, stopping 32 shots, to earn the win in goal. Vincent Trocheck and Barrett Hayton replied for Utah (10-9-3), with Karel Vejmelka taking the netminding loss, stopping 21 of 24 shots. The teams battled through a scoreless first period, with Utah outshooting Vancouver 7-4. The Mammoth continued to carry the play in the second, but Tolopilo held firm and the Canucks opened the scoring on the power play at 15:05. Boeser (who extended his point-scoring streak to eight games) made a nice cross-crease pass to DeBrusk, who tapped in his sixth goal of the season. Late in the period, Vancouver’s Linus Karlsson had a glorious chance to put the Canucks up 2-0, but he was robbed by Vejmelka who made a miraculous stick save. Utah pulled even at 2:50 of the third, as Trocheck finished a power-play give-and-go with Logan Cooley for his fourth goal of the year. Chytil restored Vancouver’s lead less than two minutes later with a wraparound tally, his third goal of the year, all in the last two games. Hayton tied things at 2-2, snapping a shot past Tolopilo from the right offensive faceoff circle at 11:39, his fourth goal of the season. Boeser made it 3-2 for Vancouver on the power play at 15:37, pouncing on a loose puck to the right of Vejmelka and depositing his eighth goal of the season. Utah pulled Vejmelka in favour of an extra attacker with two-and-a-half minutes to play but could not beat Tolopilo despite a wild scramble in front as time expired. **NOTES**: The Canucks were 2-for-4 on the power play, while the Mammoth went 1-for-5…

But it was Bradley who earned a spot in the final and helped his team to a Grey Cup win. Smith coached both brothers on the team in 2016 when they reached the Subway Bowl B.C. AA Senior Varsity Football final, falling 35-15 to the Seaquam Seahawks of Delta. 47a166da9a8c33ebdf9834b2dfb3415e.text: GoFundMe is asking people to consider certain questions before choosing to donate to a fundraiser. GoFundMe is reminding residents to take precautions before donating to a fundraiser after a charity in Summerland was allegedly scammed. The charity, New Beginnings Animal Sanctuary Society, posted on Facebook, claiming that a woman raised funds for Bald Range wildfire victims under its name through the GoFundMe platform and refused to give the money raised back to the charity. According to the post, the woman went door-to-door under the pretense of raising money for wildfire victims, along with the online fundraising platform she had already set up. “When I eventually asked about receiving the donated funds so we could purchase some of the supplies needed to get the mobile ready, I was initially given an explanation about difficulties accessing the money and told it would take another four or five days,” wrote Jane Long-Haggerty, President of New Beginnings Animal Sanctuary Society. “When I followed up, the explanation changed. I was then told that the money was needed to cover her expenses, including travel and project management costs, and that this had been disclosed in the GoFundMe description.” Since the initial post, the charity has posted multiple updates about the situation, mentioning missing and delayed funds among other things. It has also filed an RCMP report against the person. A GoFundMe spokesperson said the website has zero tolerance for the misuse of its platform, “When suspicious activity is flagged—whether through our tools, our community, or simply because a fundraiser starts gaining momentum—our dedicated experts will immediately investigate to verify its legitimacy.” In the case that answers to these questions are missing from the fundraiser, GoFundMe encourages people to message the organizer by clicking the envelope icon next to their name to ask for more information. Consequently, if there are concerns, residents can click the Report

aade2dec5d829da3581c4007e8bbce5c.text: Vancouver Police headquarters on Friday, Oct. 24, 2025, in Vancouver. A 27-year-old man is facing a charge of break-and-enter after being found on a 12-year-old girl’s bed. James Watts is charged with one count of break-and-enter in connection with the Nov. 14 incident in East Vancouver, according to a news release from the Vancouver Police Department Monday (Nov. 16). Police were called to the East Vancouver home around 6:30 a.m. on Saturday for a report from a mother that an unknown man had climbed through an unlocked basement window into her 12-year-old daughter’s bedroom. The girl was inside the room at the time. The mother heard the daughter scream and she went into the room where she found the man sitting on her daughter’s bed, police said. The mother allegedly confronted him, “forcing him to leave the residence,” the release says. Police found the man matching the description of the suspect and took him into custody without incident. “Everyone deserves to feel safe in their own home, and having an intruder enter a child’s bedroom is every parent’s worst nightmare,” Const. Darren Wong said. “We are thankful no one was injured, and we are urging everyone to ensure their windows and doors remain locked at all times. In the event an incident like this happens, contact 911 immediately.”

49bb8d29326669e3d5fb8fe28a7651a1.text: Incoming B.C. premier Doerkson says there will be no fall legislative session | Williams Lake Tribune Incoming B.C. premier Doerkson says there will be no fall legislative session Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson on Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026. Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson says there will be no fall legislative session as the new Conservative government gets its bearings in the short window between being sworn in and the holiday season. “Our government has an ambitious agenda, and we want to ensure legislation is properly prepared and receives the debate and consideration it deserves,” Doerkson said in a written statement on Monday (Nov. 16). The B.C. Conservative Party will have a large majority in the legislature when it does convene, after the party won 64 of 93 seats in the Oct. 24 election. Doerkson had left the door open to recalling the legislature for a short session before the end of the year as he seeks to pursue a slate of changes after nine years of NDP government. Conservative MLAs are scheduled to be sworn in on Thursday evening. The premier and cabinet will then be sworn in on Friday, officially taking the reins of the B.C. government. “Ministers will get to work from day one, advancing our priorities and preparing a substantive legislative agenda for the spring,” Doerkson said. The incoming government can accomplish a lot simply by taking administrative control of the various government ministries and by issuing cabinet orders. This could include changes to the Massey Tunnel project. Doerkson has promised to scrap the tunnel and build a bridge instead. The new government could also get started building other infrastructure, like the promised urgent care centres and Surrey women’s and children’s hospital. Other major campaign promises will need to wait, like the promised repeal of the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, or alterations to B.C.’s no-fault car insurance rules. These will require legislation.

ae421c0baa269e41202a074ad53e3dac.text: Telus is backing out of a partnership to build two Vancouver data centres. Telus is backing out of a partnership to build two data centres in Vancouver. “Telus has decided not to proceed with co-developing two previously announced Vancouver data centres with Westbank,” a company spokesperson said via email. “We are proceeding with the projects as planned, with a new partnership that will be announced in the coming months,” a Westbank spokesperson said. The data centres are planned for the Mount Pleasant and downtown Vancouver neighbourhoods, and will draw 150 megawatts. The excess heat generated from the centres is to be used to heat homes. Ottawa is supporting the projects through a program aimed at creating sovereign data centre infrastructure. And BC Hydro is making a $90-million upgrade to the local Mount Pleasant electrical substation to provide more power to the area’s residential and commercial customers. While it is no longer pursuing this project, a Telus spokesperson said the company remains “aligned” with the federal sovereign data centre initiative. Telus is actively expanding a facility in Kamloops and “evaluating new development partners and strategic locations to support the long-term expansion of our sovereign compute capabilities in B.C.” B.C. Green Party Leader Emily Lowan celebrated the Telus decision, crediting the No AI Vancouver protest campaign. “From day one, Vancouverites, British Columbians, and the B.C. Greens have opposed these AI data centres because they’ve been pushed through with no public accountability, and because we see them for what they are: another way for big tech to plunder our public assets and drive up costs for working people,” she said in a news release. The B.C. Green Party wants a moratorium on new data centres in B.C. Currently, the only restrictions relate to the amount of power BC Hydro can supply to all new data centre projects each year combined, limiting the power supply to 200 megawatts per year for two years,

3a99a292458feeaa801600acf7989369.text: Search and Rescue volunteers are searching for a second person after rescuing one when a fishing boat capsized Friday (Nov. 13) afternoon. The search continues for a second person who is missing after a fishing boat capsized near Yale. The Hope RCMP had responded to a report of a man yelling for help while floating in the Fraser River near the Yale tunnel at about 2:20 p.m. on Friday, Nov. 13. Police learned the fishing boat overturned and the occupants were unaccounted for. RCMP Air 1 and Hope Search and Rescue attended to the area and located a man an hour after the initial report. The man was transported safely to shore and then to hospital for treatment The Hope RCMP describe the missing man as a 60-year-old man. He is not yet accounted for. “Hope RCMP would like to thank our partner agencies for their assistance. Our thoughts are with the missing man’s family and loved ones as search efforts continue,” said Hope RCMP spokesperson Cpl. Carmen Kiener. Hope Search and Rescue (HSAR) has rescued one person and continues to search for another after a fishing boat capsized in Yale. HSAR was tasked out on Friday (Nov. 13) afternoon with news of the capsized boat. RCMP’s Air One located a person from the air and swiftwater rescuers were able to launch a boat and rescue the person. The subject told HSAR there was another person in the water. As of Saturday evening, the second person has not been located. HSAR jet boat members search above the point the boat was capsized down to Hope while others searched by air until sundown. Kent Search and Rescue and Valley Helicopter assisted in the search efforts. **News** **Incoming B.C. premier Doerkson says there will be no fall legislative session**](https://wltribune.com/2026/11/16/incoming-b-c-premier-doerkson-says-there-will-be-no-fall-legislative-session/)

Squamish RCMP is reminding people to be cautious on and around waterways after four deaths in as many days in the region. A 29-year-old woman from Squamish is dead after her kayak capsized in the Cheakamus River, just north of Squamish on Sunday. Squamish RCMP received a request to help B.C. Ambulance Service around 2:30 p.m. on Sunday (Nov. 15) with two capsized kayakers, according to a news release Monday. The kayakers were in a larger group on the Cheakamus River and went ahead from the group and capsized. Squamish Search and Rescue was called in after first responders learned that one kayaker has been found safely by the group, but another kayaker remained missing. She was found further downstream by search teams and died at the scene. This was the fourth death in as many days on Squamish waterways. Three people died in a boating incident in the Squamish Valley just days earlier. Squamish RCMP responded to that boating incident on Nov. 12. Initially, two people were found dead and a third was unaccounted for, while all others had been rescued. The third person was found dead on Nov. 13 after the search had to be suspended due to poor conditions the day before. Squamish RCMP Staff Sgt. Sascha Banks stressed that people should assess the safety of waterways before taking part in any activities on or around rivers, lakes and the ocean. “We have seen incredibly high water levels, extensive debris in the river systems, and flow rates rarely experienced in recent memory,” Banks said. “We are asking people to exercise extensive caution, conduct trip planning, check weather forecasts, tides, prepare cold-water safety gear, wear appropriate (personal flotation devices) and be prepared for emergencies.” **Regional News** **B.C. boy helps Edmonton

7d104a7a451af59878d3d8cdf441962e.text: Fill shoe boxes with toys, cloths and craft supplies to children overseas this Christmas through Evangelical Free Church for this year’s Operation Christmas Child drive. The deadline's Nov. 22. Williams Lake residents have until Sunday, Nov. 22 to drop off gift-filled shoeboxes at Evangelical Free Church for this year’s Operation Christmas Child drive. Kathy Shetler, a Williams Lake volunteer with Operation Christmas Child, has been involved since the mid 1990s when she began packing shoeboxes at Maranatha Christian School in Williams Lake. She has since helped lead the project locally, coordinate drop-offs and work with churches. Shetler said Williams Lake shipped 451 shoeboxes in 2025, with about 50 more donated online. She hopes to match or exceed last year’s in-person total. Operation Christmas Child is a Samaritan’s Purse project that works with local churches and ministries overseas to distribute gift-filled shoeboxes to children at Christian outreach events. Shetler suggested packing school supplies, hygiene items, a toy or craft kit and something to wear, such as a hat or gloves. Donors can choose to pack for a child ages two to four, five to nine or 10 to 14. Shetler asked donors to leave out candy, liquids, toothpaste, soap, glass items and war-themed toys. Shetler thanked Williams Lake residents for their generosity over the years. “It’s such an expression of love and compassion to children around the world that do not have much,” she said. Empty shoeboxes and brochures are available at the Evangelical Free Church, 1100 North 11th Ave., and at Kit and Kaboodle, 83A Second Ave. S. Filled shoeboxes can be dropped off at the church through Sunday, Nov. 22. Shetler said the boxes will travel through Kamloops to Calgary, where they’ll be checked before being shipped overseas.

280c2b8932d514fc67c76b3c88797419.text: Five years behind bars and a restitution order for $800,000 was the sentence handed down to a Kelowna woman on Nov. 17 for fraud. Lorna Eng appeared before Justice Steven Wilson in Kelowna Supreme Court on the Tuesday afternoon to learn her fate. The woman was found guilty of fraud and theft over $5,000 by a jury, after taking $844,536.13 from her former employer, Nexus Dock and Marina, between 2015 and 2019 while working as the business manager and bookkeeper. Eng was found to have been diverting customer payments through online transfers to her personal bank account, diverting customer cheques to her personal bank account and issuing business cheques to herself using pre-signed cheques left in the company’s office for business use. It was also heard that Eng attempted to conceal the transactions by using different names and email addresses not recognized by her employers. The court heard that Eng’s fraudulent activity was not detected until an external accountant and bookkeeper was hired in 2019. Eng resigned from the company in May or June of that year. At trial, Eng argued that some transfers of money from Nexus into her account were under the direction of her employer to circumvent third parties, such as the Canada Revenue Agency. She also claimed police had failed to conduct a thorough investigation into all bank accounts and credit cards, including that of her employer, and that the prosecution had not proven the charges beyond a reasonable doubt. As a result of financial challenges, Nexus closed in 2019, selling off assets and laying off 12 employees. “He described the emotional toll to have been immense and he spent a lot of time trying to understand how these circumstances could have arisen,” Justice Wilson said about a victim impact statement provided by one of the business owners. dc56bb67037fa680f0226819b8fefe5f.text: A coordinated police response led to the arrest of a woman wanted in Alberta, driving at dangerous speeds through Greater Victoria, sometimes exceeding 180 km/h. According to Sidney/North Saanich RCMP, the incident occurred shortly before 1:30 a.m. on Nov. 14 when officers attempted to conduct an impaired driving check stop in North Saanich. The driver, identified as 34-year-old Jasmine Ann Scott, fled at high speed, said an RCMP news release. Because of public safety concerns, officers did not pursue Scott, instead immediately coordinating a response with neighbouring police agencies. “It is alleged the suspect vehicle travelled through several jurisdictions at dangerous speeds, at times exceeding 180 km/h,” police said. “Through a coordinated regional response involving Sidney/North Saanich RCMP, Central Saanich Police Service, and West Shore RCMP, officers monitored the vehicle, shared real-time information, and used automated licence plate recognition technology to locate it several hours later.” Using a tire deflation device, West Shore RCMP successfully brought the vehicle to a controlled stop on the Malahat Highway, shortly after 3:30 a.m. The vehicle’s two occupants were arrested without incident. Scott has been charged with dangerous driving and flight from police. She was also arrested on multiple outstanding Alberta warrants. Anyone who witnessed a white Nissan Rogue travelling at excessive speeds on Highway 17 or the Malahat Highway during the early morning hours of Nov. 14, and has not yet spoken with police, is asked to contact Sidney/North Saanich RCMP at 250-656-3931 and quote file 2026-5998.

c0df65c332ea90abf74eb5dd92bf1a94.text: Police in Nanaimo investigated after Yasin Khan was shot and killed there in May 2021. Ronald Joseph Campbell, 42, was subsequently arrested. The victim of a 2021 gangland slaying in Nanaimo was also the target of a previous attempt on his life just months before in Langley, a court heard earlier this month. On Nov. 4, Ronald Joseph Campbell, 42, was found guilty of first-degree murder in the May 20, 2021 killing of Yasin Khan. Khan was shot while parked in a BMW SUV outside a Wendy’s at a Nanaimo shopping centre. Justice Douglas Thompson said that while there was not enough evidence to say with certainty that Campbell had pulled the trigger, he was involved in aiding and facilitating the murder plot. It was the second time in five months that someone had tried to kill Khan, the court learned. As part of Thompson’s summary of the case, he noted that Khan was one of two men who ran from a bullet-riddled Dodge Durango on Jan. 30, 2021, in Langley. The Langley Advance Times reported at the time that the shooting took place around the 7000-block of 196A Street near the Langley-Surrey border, at around 7:30 p.m. Inside the Durango, police found drug-dealing paraphernalia, including multiple phones that were ringing with drug orders, according to Thompson’s summary. Both men who had been in the Durango survived unharmed, but they refused to help police, according to local investigators. The same man who had been with Khan during the Langley shooting was with him, in another car parked next to his, during the fatal shooting in Nanaimo. That man is not named in the court record. There was no indication whether the Langley shooting was directly linked to the Nanaimo shooting, or whether any of the same people were involved. Campbell, who was working for the Bacon Brothers gang in early 2021, has been sentenced to life in prison with no possibility of parole for 25 years, the automatic sentence for first-degree murder.

252f8b417262611be3a1ad36a2eeeb78.text: B.C. pop star Carly Rae Jepsen to host 2027 JUNO Awards | Williams Lake Tribune Mission's Carly Rae Jepsen will host and perform at the 2027 JUNO Awards in Winnipeg on April 4. Mission’s Carly Rae Jepsen is set to host the 2027 JUNO Awards in Winnipeg. The Canadian Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences (CARAS) and CBC announced Jepsen as host on Nov. 9, with the show scheduled for April 4 at Canada Life Centre. According to a news release, the three-time JUNO winner from Mission will bring her signature pop sound to the stage while leading the festivities as host for the first time. In addition to Jepsen, the show will feature performances from Angine De Poitrine, Our Lady Peace, and more. Allan Reid, the president/CEO of CARAS and the JUNO Awards, said the lineup brings together artists who have helped shape the sound of Canadian music alongside those pushing it in exciting new directions. “From celebrating the incredible legacy of Our Lady Peace to welcoming Carly Rae Jepsen as our host, we can’t wait to share these moments with fans in Winnipeg and across the country,” Reid said. Jepsen earned Album of the Year and Pop Album of the Year at the 2013 JUNO Awards for her 2012 album, *Kiss.* The hit “Call Me Maybe” took home Single of the Year at the same awards. In September, the Mission pop star released her 8th studio album, *Day and Night*. It included the singles “On Wire”, “Motivation”, and “Don’t Leave Me on the Dance Floor.” The 24-track double album was inspired by a period of personal transformation and reflects Jepsen’s continued creative evolution and willingness to explore new musical directions. Per the release, it explores two sides of her artistry, blending “sun-soaked, folk-leaning pop with after-hours dance music”. Jepsen’s “Day and Night Tour” kicks off over a week after the JUNOs, including a show at The Orpheum in Vancouver on April 18.

9d0fb319854b44cd96bc9386a0f773bc.text: Teck's mine at Highland Valley near Logan Lake is the largest open-pit copper mine in Canada. B.C.’s Labour Relations Board has partially sided with a union in its bid to seek remedies for non-bargaining workers doing the work of union members. Board vice-chair Paul Todd released his decision Friday (Nov. 13), following a four-day hearing between the United Steelworkers Local 7619 and Teck’s Highland Valley Copper mine. The United Steelworkers Local 7619 alleged Teck’s Highland Valley Copper was breaching two sections of the Labour Relations Code – sections 6(3)(e) and 68 – by using ineligible replacement workers and contractors to perform the work of employees who are currently on strike. The union represents 1,200 employees at the mine. The union initially claimed the employer breached code in seven instances, but following pre-hearing discussions, it was narrowed down to five instances. The union was seeking remedies that included a declaration, a cease-and-desist order, damages and an order to have a designated union representative access the worksite. Teck operates Highland Valley Copper mine, which is about 17 kilometres west of Logan Lake. The company began a large construction project in August 2025 to expand and extend the life of the mine. According to the decision, the project construction work is “largely” performed by contractors and not members of the bargaining unit. Teck and Local 7619’s collective agreement expired on Sept. 30. The union members voted in favour of a strike on Oct. 19, with job action beginning on Oct. 24. The project area, according to the decision, is a common site for picketing. Todd found Teck breached Section 68 of the Labour Relations Code by having three workers perform work meant to be done by bargaining employees, as well as having a contractor do some road work. d94f3bc87ca2114bbedefc6ca017afd3.text: Sgt. Freda Fong, with the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT), announced the arrest of two people in a fatal shooting in September 2025 in Langley. Tushar Sharma was found dead in a burning car near Fort Langley in late October. Homicide investigators are asking for tips. Firefighters discovered human remains while investigating a vehicle fire in Fort Langley last month, and now homicide investigators have taken over the investigation. Tushar Sharma, a 25-year-old Surrey man, has been identified as the victim by the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT). Sharma’s body was found on Oct. 29 when RCMP and firefighters responded to a report of a car on fire in the 23300-block of Rawlison Crescent. The site is just south of the village of Fort Langley in a rural area. The deceased man does not have a criminal record, and according to IHIT, he had limited known contacts in Canada. “IHIT investigators continue to work with Mr. Sharma’s family and friends in Canada and overseas to gain a better understanding of his lifestyle and activities leading up to his death,” said Sgt. Freda Fong, of IHIT. “While the motive remains under investigation, evidence to date suggests this was a targeted incident.” IHIT is working with the Langley RCMP and the Integrated Forensic Identification Services unit, along with the BC Coroners Service to determine what happened to Sharma. The homicide investigators are working to put together a timeline of the events leading up to Sharma’s death. Anyone with information is asked to contact IHIT at 1-877-551-IHIT (4448) or by email at ihitinfo@rcmp-grc.gc.ca.

aaa84fe4aae62506e240bbf9961dda9c.text: A 28-year-old man is facing multiple charges after Quesnel RCMP located a stolen pickup truck from Agassiz, B.C. According to an RCMP press release, at approximately 4:23 a.m. on Nov. 13, police located a stolen Doge Ram pickup truck in Quesnel. A man was seen fleeing from the vehicle in the 300-block of Doherty Drive. Officers located and arrested Kyle Fredrick Ford a short distance away. Mounties said Ford has been held in custody and charged with possession of stolen property, prohibited driving and two counts of failing to comply with conditions.

02f26c80dc370a7e9dad29172d470d51.text: Quesnel RCMP seized a handgun, thousands of dollars in cash and several suspected illegal drugs during the arrest of a 33-year-old man. According to an RCMP press release, Mounties arrested the man at approximately 4:15 p.m. on Nov. 12 in the 400-block of Willis Street in Quesnel. RCMP said during the arrest, officers seized a 9mm handgun, approximately $13,000 in cash, 102.7 grams of suspected fentanyl, 48 grams of suspected crack cocaine and 84 grams of methamphetamine as well as miscellaneous pills. Mounties said the man has since been released pending further investigation.
